name: Michael Bloomberg

controls.name: Bloomberg L.P. (financial data, Terminal, Bloomberg News/Media)
controls.role: Co-founder (1981); majority owner; Vlad Kliatchko CEO since 2023

controls.name: Bloomberg Businessweek (acquired 2009), BloombergNEF (New Energy Finance, 2009), Bloomberg Industry Group / BNA (acquired 2011 for $990M)

stakes.name: Baltimore Orioles (MLB) — investor in the David Rubenstein-led group that bought control from the Angelos family ($1.725B for the control stake incl. MASN stake); MLB owners approved unanimously

vehicles.name: Bloomberg L.P.
vehicles.notes: Private operating company; EDGAR registrant (NY). Merrill Lynch's remaining 20% bought back in 2008 for a reported $4.43B.

vehicles.name: Bloomberg Inc.
vehicles.notes: Bloomberg corporate entity registered on EDGAR (NY); filing types not reviewed.

vehicles.name: Bloomberg-BNA Holdings Inc.
vehicles.notes: Vehicle linked to 2011 BNA acquisition (per EDGAR registrant name).

privateDeals.what: Bloomberg L.P. extended its leases at 731 Lexington Ave (~947,000 sq ft) by 11 years, from Feb 2029 to Feb 2040. Bloomberg paid landlord Alexander's Inc. $129.3M in 2025, about 61% of Alexander's rental revenue

trophies.what: Media outlets via Bloomberg L.P.: Bloomberg News, Bloomberg Businessweek, Bloomberg TV
Minority stake in the Baltimore Orioles (Rubenstein group)

policy.what: Past Bloomberg L.P. legal matters: construction fraud schemes involving executives/subcontractors (2018-2021) and workplace discrimination suits (older)
Appointed UN Secretary-General's Special Envoy on Climate Ambition and Solutions (2021-02-05); earlier UN climate envoy roles in 2014 and 2018
Bloomberg Philanthropies funds the UNFCCC secretariat to cover US funding gaps after Paris Agreement withdrawals (e.g., up to $15M pledge in 2017)
Bloomberg L.P. is the sole office tenant of 731 Lexington Avenue (Alexander's Inc.; 952,000 sq ft office), and Alexander's calls it its significant tenant

giving.name: Bloomberg Family Foundation Inc. (vehicle behind Bloomberg Philanthropies; ~$12.1B assets FY2024)

Bloomberg Philanthropies (CEO Patti Harris): $1B Johns Hopkins medical school free-tuition gift (2024); $600M to four historically Black medical schools (Aug 2024); $100M pledge to Global Polio Eradication Initiative (Dec 2025)
Lifetime giving ~$25.4B incl. $4.3B in 2025; pledged Bloomberg LP stake to his foundation upon death; Giving Pledge signer (2010)
Bloomberg Family Foundation Inc. — total assets $11.81B, revenue $1.51B, expenses $1.43B (FY2023 Form 990-PF)

watch.what: Bloomberg L.P. board chair succession after Mark Carney's departure (Carney became chair in 2023, listed as 2023-2025)
Bloomberg Family Foundation next Form 990-PF filing (FY2025) showing size of 2025 giving ($4.3B per Forbes)
Long-term ownership transition: Bloomberg LP stake pledged to his foundation on death
Alexander's Inc. 10-Qs/10-K disclose Bloomberg's rent and credit monitoring as its largest tenant

gaps: Willett Advisors LLC (EDGAR CIK 0001509379, New York) last filed a 13F in 2014. No filing seen ties it to Bloomberg by name, so it is not listed as his vehicle. Still Wikipedia-sourced and not retracted: Bloomberg L.P. subsidiaries/legal history, the board-chair watch item and the Bloomberg Philanthropies gifts. Real estate is still not verified from reputable reporting.
